artists.biography:
The Beloved are an English electronic dance music group, best known for the singles "Sweet Harmony", "The Sun Rising", "Hello", "Your Love Takes Me Higher", "Satellite" and "Deliver Me".
In 1982 Jon Marsh was playing drums for Twelve of August. He met Cambridge University graduate Steve Waddington when he joined Twelve of August as an additional guitarist (other members were Steve Seale (Barrington) and John Seale). When Twelve of August split Jon and Steve formed Journey Through.
Jon Marsh and Steve Waddington following the break up off the band Twelve of August formed the core of a band named Journey Through (the name taken from a line of the song 'Heaven in Love', written by Steve Seale and Jo Caney). The pair were joined by Tim Havard. When Guy Gausden later joined the band, the group changed their name to The Beloved. The band originally had a guitar-oriented sound, but soon began using drum machines and dance music elements. They sounded at times like post-punk/dance group New Order, and a summation of this stage of their career can be found on their first studio album, Where It Is, which is a compilation of previously released material, consisting of singles and related B-Sides, pressed onto one individual long playing work. The record includes all the early singles, "A Hundred Words", "This Means War", "Happy Now", and the double A-side "Surprise Me" / "Forever Dancing", all released between 1986 and 1987, all on Where It Is, all making the Top 30 in the UK Indie Chart, and all failing in the UK Top 75.

perplexity.description:
Released in 1990, Happiness is the debut studio album by British electronic duo The Beloved, comprising Jon Marsh and Steve Waddington. The album marks a pivotal shift in the band’s sound, moving away from their earlier guitar-driven indie style toward a vibrant fusion of acid house, pop, and techno, shaped by their immersion in London’s burgeoning club scene. Featuring lush synthesizers, danceable rhythms, and guest vocals from Chicago house diva Kym Mazelle, Happiness captures the euphoric energy of the post-acid house era, with standout tracks like “The Sun Rising,” “Hello,” and “Your Love Takes Me Higher” blending melodic pop sensibilities with club-oriented production.

Happiness stands as the only album released by The Beloved as a duo and is widely regarded as their definitive work. It was a commercial breakthrough, reaching #14 on the UK Albums Chart and spawning three Top 40 singles, including the international hit “Hello.” The album’s success helped establish The Beloved as key figures in the UK’s electronic pop movement, and its influence extended beyond the charts, inspiring a remix companion album, Blissed Out, in 1991. Critically, Happiness was praised for its innovative blend of dance and pop, appealing to both ravers and mainstream audiences, and remains a landmark release in the band’s discography.
